items.text: IMPORTANT PERSONALITIES OF MUMBAI AND MODERN INDIA
Grade 8 ICSE Social Studies (Mumbai) | Notes + Comparative Table + Practice Questions
QUICK REVISION NOTES
Jamsetji Nusserwanji Tata (1839–1904) – Father of Indian Industry

Graduated from Elphinstone College, Mumbai (1858); founded a trading firm in 1868 and converted an oil mill at Chinchpokli, Mumbai (1869) into the Alexandra cotton mill, later establishing Bombay's Swadeshi Mill.
items.topic: Jamsetji Nusserwanji Tata (1839–1904) – Father of Indian Industry

items.text: Opened the Taj Mahal Hotel at Colaba waterfront, Mumbai (3 December 1903, first in India with electricity) and laid foundations for Tata Steel, IISc Bengaluru, and Tata Power.
items.topic: Jamsetji Nusserwanji Tata (1839–1904) – Father of Indian Industry

items.text: Mahatma Jyotirao Phule (1827–1890) – Pioneer of Social Equality
Social reformer and writer in Maharashtra who championed equal rights for marginalized communities, farmers, mill workers, and women (Britannica).
items.topic: Mahatma Jyotirao Phule (1827–1890) – Pioneer of Social Equality

items.text: Founded the Satyashodhak Samaj (Society of Truth Seekers) in 1873 to promote social justice without priestly intermediaries.
items.topic: Mahatma Jyotirao Phule (1827–1890) – Pioneer of Social Equality

items.text: Savitribai Phule (1831–1897) – Pioneer of Women's Education in Maharashtra
Regarded as India's first female teacher; worked alongside Jyotirao Phule to open indigenous schools for girls (starting in 1848) and shelter destitute widows (Britannica).
items.topic: Savitribai Phule (1831–1897) – Pioneer of Women's Education in Maharashtra

items.text: Dr. Bhimrao Ramji Ambedkar (1891–1956) – Architect of the Indian Constitution

Jurist, economist, and reformer (Britannica) whose Mumbai residence, Rajgriha (Dadar), anchored his civic and educational movements; chaired the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly of India.
items.topic: Dr. Bhimrao Ramji Ambedkar (1891–1956) – Architect of the Indian Constitution

items.text: Raja Ram Mohan Roy (1772–1833) – Father of the Indian Renaissance
Founded the Brahmo Sabha in 1828 (precursor to Brahmo Samaj), inspiring Bombay's Prarthana Samaj; campaigned for the Abolition of Sati (1829) and modern scientific education (Britannica).
items.topic: Raja Ram Mohan Roy (1772–1833) – Father of the Indian Renaissance

items.text: COMPARATIVE TABLE – EASY TO REMEMBER
PRACTICE QUESTIONS & ANSWER KEY
Which Mumbai hotel opened on 3 December 1903 as India's first with electricity?
items.answer: The Taj Mahal Hotel at Colaba waterfront, founded by Jamsetji Tata.

items.text: Which society was founded in 1873 by Jyotirao Phule and supported by Savitribai Phule?
items.answer: The Satyashodhak Samaj (Society of Truth Seekers).

items.text: Name the Mumbai residence of Dr. B. R. Ambedkar and the organization founded by Raja Ram Mohan Roy in 1828.
items.answer: Rajgriha in Dadar (Mumbai) and the Brahmo Sabha (1828).

items.text: Why did Jawaharlal Nehru call Jamsetji Tata a One-Man Planning Commission?
items.answer: Because he pioneered India's core steel, hydroelectric power, and technical education institutions.

items.text: Remember the 5 Pioneers in order — Jamsetji Tata (Industry) → Jyotirao Phule (Truth) → Savitribai Phule (Schools) → Ambedkar (Constitution) → Roy (Renaissance).
